title: Integration of Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs for Complex Reasoning
summary: This community centers on the convergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Knowledge Graphs (KGs) to address complex question answering and reasoning tasks. It highlights a shift from traditional multi-hop KBQA methods to autonomous agent frameworks and unified reasoning paradigms. Key contributions include survey papers defining the roadmap for LLM-KG integration and specific methods like KG-Agent and UniKGQA that enhance faithfulness and interpretability in graph-based reasoning.
key_findings: The paper 'Unifying Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs: A Roadmap' (IEEE TKDE 2024) provides a comprehensive framework for integrating LLMs with KGs, authored by a team including Shirui Pan, Linhao Luo, and Xindong Wu.

KG-Agent is an efficient autonomous agent framework proposed by Kun Zhou, Wayne Xin Zhao, and others for complex reasoning over knowledge graphs, representing a methodological advancement in this domain.

UniKGQA, published at ICLR 2023, is a method for unified retrieval and reasoning specifically designed to solve multi-hop question answering over knowledge graphs, developed by Kun Zhou and Wayne Xin Zhao.

The work 'Reasoning on Graphs: Faithful and Interpretable Large Language Model Reasoning' (arXiv 2024) by Linhao Luo, Yuan-Fang Li, Gholamreza Haffari, and Shirui Pan focuses on improving the faithfulness and interpretability of LLM reasoning on graphs.

Two major survey papers, 'A Survey on Complex Knowledge Base Question Answering' (IJCAI 2021) and 'Complex Knowledge Base Question Answering: A Survey' (IEEE TKDE 2023), authored by Gaole He, Wayne Xin Zhao, and Jing Jiang, document the methods, challenges, and solutions in the field.

Earlier foundational work on multi-hop QA, such as 'Improving Multi-hop Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs using Knowledge Base Embeddings' (ACL 2020) by Apoorv Saxena and Partha P. Talukdar, established the baseline for the subsequent LLM-integrated approaches.
